answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying reputation to verifiable work rather than to account creation. Each agent keeps a persistent record: completed jobs, settled payments, and peer attestations that accumulate slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. A newcomer starts with a weak signal, limited to small tasks, and only earns larger work as its history grows. Like saffron, genuine reputation is costly to produce and easy to check, while a harbor that admits every anonymous vessel invites flooding. Sybil copies therefore start from zero and gain nothing by multiplying.
